SALES TAX
SALES TAX. REFUND RULES, 1996
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part II, 22nd August, 1996]
S.R.0.695
(1)/96, dated 22‑8‑1996.‑‑In exercise of the ' powers
conferred by section 50 of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with subsection (1) and
(2) of section 10 thereof. The Central Board of Revenue is pleased to make the
following rules, namely:‑‑
1. Short title, application and commencement.‑‑(1)
These rules may be called Sales Tax Refund Rules, 1996.
(2) These
shall apply to the cases where the tax return filed by a registered person
indicates that the input tax exceeds the output tax and the excess amount is
liable to be refunded to the registered person.
(3) These
shall come into force at once.
2. Definitions.‑‑In there Rules, unless the
subject or context provide otherwise,‑‑
(i)
"Act" means the Sales Tax Act, 1990;
(ii)
"commercial exporter" means a person whose taxable activity is
confined to zero rated supplies and opts for voluntary registration under
section 18 of the Act;
(iii)
"Officer incharge" means Assistant Collector, Deputy Collector or
Additional Collector who holds charge of the Refund Section; and
(iv)
"Investor" means a person covered under the proviso to subsection (1)
of section 10 of the Act.
3. Refund section.‑‑(1) There shall be established a
Refund Section in each Collectorate of Sales . Tax to process and settle the
refund claims.
(2) The
Refund Section shall be headed by an Assistant Collector or such other senior
officer of sales tax as may be nominated by the Collector of sales tax.
4. Tax return to be treated as refund claim.‑‑(1)
Where a monthly tax return filed by a registered person indicates that input
tax exceeds the output tax such return shall be treated as a refund claim and
shall be processed accordingly.
(2) A legible
photocopy of the return referred to in sub‑rule (1) shall be forwarded to
the officer‑incharge for appropriate action under the law.
5. Receipt and scrutiny of refund claim.‑‑(1) The
officer incharge shall assign an official to receive the refund claim and enter
the relevant details in a register kept for this purpose.
(2) The
officer‑incharge shall refer the refund claim to the Auditor or Deputy
Superintendent of the sales tax for carrying out necessary scrutiny in order to
ascertain whether any refund is admissible under the law.
(3) The
Auditor or, as the case may be, Deputy Superintendent shall request the
registered person by Fax message or on telephone to furnish the following
documents:‑‑
(a) Bills
of entry and tax invoices indicating the purchases made by him.
(b) Bills
of export indicating Mate Receipt Number and date as an evidence of export of
goods;
Provided
that where information is sought over the telephone, title of the person spoken
to, time, date and brief contents of conversation shall be recorded for further
reference.
(4) The
Auditor or, as the case may be, Deputy Superintendent shall examine the refund
claim and other evidence referred to in clause (a) & (b) of sub‑rule
(3), to ascertain whether‑‑
(a) the
calculation in the tax return regarding the amount of input tax, output tax and
the amount to be refunded have been made correctly;
(b) the
amount of input tax as shown in the return is supported by tax invoice,
replacement invoice or import documents; and
(c) the
amount of output tax as shown in the return does not show a marked fall as
against the output tax reported in the returns for the last three months.
(5) The
Auditor or, as the case may be, Deputy Superintendent shall carry out necessary
scrutiny and give a report within ten days of reference to him under sub‑rule
(2) of rule (5) on the admissibility of the refund claim to the Senior Auditor
or Superintendent (Refund) who shall give his comments thereon and pass it on
to the officer‑incharge.
(6) The
officer-incharge shall examine the report and may make or cause to be made such
further enquiry as he may consider necessary.
